activities.title: Make Comparisons
activities.content:
Compare illustrations
• Show pupils how to open their Pupil Books to the 
first page. Hold up the Pupil Book so that pupils 
can see the page for Lesson 1 and point to the first 
illustration.
• Say: Waɗ honndu maa ndu ka natal ido ngal. Ngal kullal ko hoɗum? Eey ko ngal nagge.
• Point to the next picture in the row, to the right of the bull.
• Say: Mbaɗen kolli men ɗii ka natal ido. ɗum na nanndi eko aratako? Alaa!
• Point to the next picture in the row. 
• Say: Ndaaren gongal ngal. Si ngal nanndi e natal ido ngal? Alaa!
• Point to the final picture in the row. 
• Say: Si ngal nanndi e natal ido ngal? Eey!
• Continue this process with the other rows, each time asking the pupils to study the first 
illustration and find the other illustration in the row that matches.
Compare shapes
• Ask pupils to turn to the next page in the Pupil Book.
• Use the same process as the activity above with the shapes on the next page of the 
Pupil Book.

activities.title: Story sequence Starter
activities.content:
Tell a story using pictures
• Show the next page in the Pupil Book.
• Say: Mbaɗee kolli mon ka natal ido ngal. Ko hoɗum neɗɗo o waɗata?
• Call on two pupils to respond.
• Talk with pupils about each picture in the sequence (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6). Ask pupils what 
the people are doing in each picture and ask questions to help them think about the 
pictures.
• Ask pupils to look at the pictures and describe the story the pictures are telling. 
Help them see that the woman is preparing "toori".

activities.title: Trace lines
activities.content:
Follow lines with a finger
• Show the next page in the Pupil Book.
Say: Ko hoɗum suka gorko wonɗo e natal he waɗata? Wallen mbo lat de upeere nde 
he nder jala o! On parii? Mbaɗee kolli mon holliron hoto upere nde abbi.
Show pupils how to trace the line from the ball to the goal with a finger.
Say: Ko hoɗum waandu nduu waɗata? Ko hoɗum sikkuɗon ndu faala?
• Watch as pupils trace the line from the monkey to the banana with a finger.
• Repeat with the remaining image.

activities.title: Parts of a Book
activities.content:
Recognize the Grade parts of a book - cover, back, 
title
• Point to the cover and back of a book. 
Say: En fuɗɗorat janngu de ka yeeso deftere abboɗen ɓaawo. ɗum woni ɗerol yeeso deftere 
nde.
Say: Kelme ngonɗe he ɗerol yeeso deftere nde hollata en hoore jannde deftere nde. Hoore 
janngde deftere nde haalanta on kowww janngeten.
Teach and discuss vocabulary
• Tell pupils each word. Have them repeat it but do not write it on the board. Ask 
pupils what they know about each one.
• Discuss the word meaning, using gestures or illustrations to support understanding. 
If needed, help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they 
know.
kappe ,  caŋaral, debbo

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
Read the following story aloud 
• Use the appropriate big book or supplementary illustrations if available
• While reading, pause to think aloud and talk to pupils about the story at key 
moments  such as when you come to a vocabulary word the pupils just learned.

Faatu na Famɗi Nobete
Faatu welta nooki. Mbo wonno ka galle o alaa wadde hayhunde. O yi'i gorgol mum 
Kummba na una kappe fii toori.
"Gorgol, mi walle?"
"Eeh alaa, Faatu, a janngii ko heewi!" Ndeen Faatu yehi.
O yi'i denɗiraawo makko na fewnita caŋaral makko ngal ko yooɗi. "Jaaja, mi walle?"
"Eeh alaa, Faatu, a janngii ko heewi!" Ndeen Faatu yehi kadi.
Ndeen o yi'i kotoo makko gorko na rema ka faro. "Kotoo, mi walle?"
"Eeh alaa, Faatu, a janngii ko heewi!" Ndeen Faatu yehi.
O yii jaja maako kadi no jannga deftere. "Jaaja, mi walle?"
"Eeh alaa, Faatu, a janngii ko heewi!"
ɓaawo ɗum, o yahi ka baaba makko. Baaba makko lamndi mbo, "Giɗo am Faatu, ko 
hoɗɗum loobɗaa?"
"Simi unii toori mi janngii ko heewi. Simi fewnii caŋaral mi janngii ko heewi. Simi remii 
faro mi janngii ko heewi. Simi janngi defte mi janngii ko heewi. Ko hoɗum mi foti wat 
de?''
Baaba makko wi'i, "Ee Faatou! Wota loob! A mawnii jooni. Miɗo yiɗi neɗɗo mbawɗo 
kam wallude fii fewnude lemunaaje ɗe ka arkaaji. A wallat kam?" ndeen o walli mbo.

activities.title: Rapid review
activities.content:
Review the parts of a book - cover, back, title
• Call on a volunteer pupil to show the class which part of a book you start reading 
from. Ask what this part of the book it is called. (correct response: ("front page")
• Question: Hotto yiiɗon hoore jannde taalol ngol? Answer: "Ka ombaalo yeso deftere 
"
• of the story that was just read aloud.
• Question: Nde yottiɗen ka gasnirde deftere  ko hoɗum yiiɗeen?Answer:"Ombaalo 
ɓaawo deftere"
• Call on a volunteer pupil to answer and point to the back of the book.

sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Track objects from left to right with their eyes, and with a finger.

activities.title: Make Comparisons
activities.content:
Compare shapes of capital letters 
Hold up the Pupil Book so that pupils can see the page and point to the first capital letter. 
Do not say the name of the letter - this is NOT an activity for pupils to learn letters. It is 
an activity for pupils to practice telling the difference between letter and shapes.
• Say: Mina sappino hondu am ndu ka alkulal ido ngal. Wota haygooto sappino. Enndaarat 
alkulal gongal waa ngal nii 
• Point to the next one in the row.
• Say: Mbaɗen honndu men ndu he alkulal ido ngal. Si ngal nanndi he alkulal ido ngal? 
Alaa!
• Point to the next one in the row.
• Say: Ndaaren gongal ngal. Si ngal nanndi he ido ngal? 
• Point to the final one in the row. . 
• Say:  Si ngal  na nanndi he ido ngal  kadi? Eey!
• Continue this process with the other rows, each time asking the pupils to study the first 
capital letter and find the other one in the row that matches it.
Compare shapes
• Use the same process as the activity above with the small letters on the next page of 
the Pupil Book. Do not say the name of the letter - this is NOT an activity for pupils 
to learn letters. It is an activity for pupils to practice telling the difference between 
letter shapes.

activities.title: Describe differences
activities.content:
Talk about the differences between objects
• Hold up the Pupil Book so that pupils can see the four objects in the next activity. Ask 
pupils to point to the objects in their own books.
• Call on pupils to describe what images go together and why (there is no 1 correct 
answer).
  2. Trace lines  (5 mins)
Follow lines with a finger
• Say: Jokken koy kulloy! Ido o ko somre! Mbaɗen kolli men ɗi ka fuɗɗorde jokken no 
somre nde taɗɗiri ni ka ɗerol.
• Demonstrate following the line on the page as needed.
• Repeat with the remaining images.
• Say: Ngol konngol na immorii he taalol ngol mi jannguno ngol. Een haalat fii jolɗe wonɗe 
hakkunde kelme he nder kongii. Simi ɗa janngude, mi janngat helmere kala gooto gooto, 
sabu helmere kala no woodi ko firti.
• Point to a word in the sentence. Read the word and say its meaning.
• Point to the space after the word.
• Say: Jolɗe wonnɗe hakkunde kelme hollii kam hono helmere nde darori e hoto helmere 
aroore nde fuɗɗori.
• Point to the following word in the sentence. Read the word and say its meaning.
•  Say: Jolɗe wonnɗe hakkunde kelme ɗee wallat maa janngude. Si a winndii konngi 
seertuɗi, aɗa foti wadde yolnde hakkunde kelme ɗe.
• Write another sentence. Choose a volunteer to help demonstrate on the new sentence.
•  Say: Waɗ honndu maa ndu ka helmere. Jooni, hollam helmere wonnde ndee. Ko hono 
hollirtaa ko seertini hakkunde ɗe kelme ɗiɗi? (hakkunde majje na waɗi jolnɗe)
• Pick up the book. Walk around the room. Ask 3 pupils to find a space between two 
words and put their fingers on it.

• Point to the space after the word.
• Say: Jolɗe wonnɗe hakkunde kelme hollii kam hono helmere nde darori e hoto 
helmere aroore nde fuɗɗori.
• Point to the following word in the sentence. Read the word and say its meaning.

• Write another sentence. Choose a volunteer to help demonstrate on the new

• Say: Waɗ honndu maa ndu ka helmere. Jooni, hollam helmere wonnde nde. Ko hono

• Pick up the book. Walk around the room. Ask 3 pupils to find a space between two

sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Track objects from left to right with their eyes and with a finger.
Recognize sight words.
Read sentences using sight words and pictures.
Draw simple shapes.

activities.title: Read sight words
activities.content:
Learn two new sight words 
• Point to the pictures of the boy and girl in the Pupil Book.
• Say: O ko Aba. O ko Kummba. En janngat fii maɓɓe ko heewi e ngol laawol.
• Say: Mbaɗee kolli mon ɗii ka helmere (Aba) he lees natal suka gorko o. Mbaɗee 
kolli mon ɗii ka helmere (Kummba) he les natal suka debbo o..
• Point to the following activity in the Pupil Book (matching activity).
• Ask pupils to point to [Aba] on the left side, then point to the matching name on the 
right side. Repeat with [Kummba].
• Point to the following activity in the Pupil Book (box with boy and girl names).
• Ask pupils to say the first name in the left column, then point to the matching name 
in the row.
• Continue in the same way with each row.

activities.title: Read a sentence
activities.content:
Read a sentence using sight words
• Say: Mi yi'i Kummba ka dow ngol ɗerol. Jooni mi yi'i helmere hesere! Nde helmere 
hesere woni (yi'i). Sabu eɗen anndi (Kummba) e ndee helmere hesere, en waawat 
janngu ko ɗee nate firti."

• Point to the first picture sentence on the page in the Pupil Book. Ask pupils to name 
the picture on the right.
• Read the picture sentence aloud to pupils, showing them how you point to the 
pictures/word with your finger as you read.
• Continue to the next picture sentence. Ask pupils to point to the boy.
• Point to pictures or words as you read. [Aba yi'i mbeewa].
• Remind pupils that "yi'i" means "to observe" or "to see."
• Make a gesture to demonstrate seeing. Then, ask pupils to read the picture sentence 
again together.
• Say: Jooni, ko hommbo yiiɗon lees? Mbaɗen kolli men ɗii ka konngol  janngiden 
konngol ngol (Kummba yi'i taabal).
• Say: Ko hommbo waawi janngu ɗii konngi arooɗi? ?  
• Continue calling on pupils to read the picture sentences until the end of the page.

activities.title: Describe differences
activities.content:
Talk about the differences between objects 
Point to the next activity in the Pupil Book.
• Say: Waɗen kolli men ɗii ka les natal adii ngal ngal. Hoɗum yiiɗon? On yii jooɗorgal
• rewngal ngal heen? 
• Point to the next picture in the row.
• Say: Eyi, nagge! Ko hodum sertini nagge nge  mbaaluguu?
• Continue with other illustrations.

activities.title: Draw shapes
activities.content:
Practice drawing common shapes
• Ask pupils to trace each shape in the Pupil Book with one finger.
• Ask pupils to try to draw 3 of each shape in their exercise books. Depending on 
their comfort with writing and drawing, different pupils may focus on just one 
shape or draw many.

sessions.title: Session B
learning_outcomes: Track objects from left to right with  their eyes and with a finger.
Use new words correctly in sentences.
Use verbal and non-verbal communication appropriately.

activities.title: How to read – track with a finger
activities.content:
Teach how to track words with a finger 
•  Say:  Simi janngii, mi ndaarat helmere kala. Helmere fof no waɗi ko nde firti. 
Faamgol ko janngoton ko no wonndi e nafoore he janngugol helmere kala. Waɗee 
kooli mondu e lees helmere kala nde janngoton, ɗum wallat on wota on taɗɗu kelme 
goɗɗe.
• Write a sentence on the board. Demonstrate how to track with your finger under 
each word as you read. Be sure to place and pause your finger under the specific 
word.
• Call on a pupil at random to describe what to do with a finger while reading.
• Call on 2 pupils to demonstrate tracking words of the sentence on the board while 
you read it aloud.

activities.title: Vocabulary – before reading
activities.content:
Teach and discuss vocabulary
• Tell pupils each word. Have them repeat it but do not write it on the board. Ask 
pupils what they know about each one.
• Discuss the word meaning, using gestures or illustrations to support understanding. 
If needed, help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they 
know.
   ñawndoowo, jonntinooje, neene

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
Reread the following story aloud 
• Use the appropriate big book or supplementary illustrations if available
• Partway through the story, pause to show pupils how you track reading with your 
finger below each word you read as you read it. At the end of the line of text, make 
a big sweeping motion back to the start of the next line of text. Continue tracking 
with your finger.
• After demonstrating, complete the read aloud.
Adamayel Heɓi Jontinooje
Aadamayel no wondi he Neene mum e Baaba mum.
Neene e Baaba noddi mo, Aadamaa!" suudu ndu na d e ƴ ƴ � i .  ɓ e  n a n a a n i 
haygooto jaabiiɗo. Hotto Aadama?
Aadama nani neene mum e baaba mum na nodda. Aadama nootaaki. O kontini lelagol 
ka mbalndi.
Neene e Baaba ndaarondiri. Neene dogi naati ka suudu Aadama.
Neene wi'i, "Aadama, jam waali, hono ɓanndu ndu?" Aadama jaabii, "Ee neene, neene 
mi sellaani! "Neene waɗi junngo makko ngo ka tiinde Aadama o wi'i, "ɓanndu ma ndu 
na wuli! Mi noddat ñawndoowo o!" Baaba noddi ñawndoowo o.
Ñawndoowo ari ndaarde Aadama o wi'i, "Aɗa heɓi ɓanndu wulndu! Fado men ñawndam 
aa!" Reedu Aadama ndu muusi, o lamndi, "Ñawndoowo, Ñawndoowo! Mi maayat na?"
Ñawndoowo o jali o wi'i, "Alaa, Aadama! Mi okkat ma lekki a ɗaanoto!"
Neene wi'i, "ñawndoowo o a jaraama!" Ñawndoowo wi'i, "wota yejjit lekki kii. Gila 
hannde haa yeeso, Aadama no foti lelaade e lees sanke!"
Neene ndaari Baaba o wi'i, "Sooden sanke hannde! Wakkilo, dog to marse to!" Aadama 
nani ɓe haala o leltii.
Ngol taalol na holliri fii dandugol jontinooje e ñawndugol sukaaɓe, ɗum na hollira nafa 
ɗaɓugol cellal e lelaade he lees sankeeji.

activities.title: Vocabulary – after reading
activities.content:
Check for vocabulary understanding
• Ask pupils if they heard the new vocabulary words during the read aloud.
• Call on 3-4 pupils to say what vocabulary word they heard and to say the meaning 
in their own words.
• Say: Jooni naftoren kelme ɗe janngunoɗen fii fewnen konngi.

• Give an example by using one of the words in a new sentence - one that is not in 
the pupil book or read aloud.
• For each other vocabulary word introduced before reading, ask a pupil to use the 
word in a new sentence. Have pupils act out a word, if appropriate. Congratulate, 
help, or correct the pupils, depending on the responses.

activities.title: Rapid review
activities.content:
Review tracking words with a finger
• Ask a volunteer pupil to tell you something you should do to be sure you don't 
skip words while reading. (Correct response - track the words with your finger, or 
follow under the words with your finger, etc.)
• Ask one pupil to demonstrate tracking for the class using the book.

activities.title: Read a sentence using sight words
activities.content:
Talk about the differences between objects
• Ask pupils to try to read the picture sentences using the sight words they learned

pupil at random to read the first sentence. Ask another pupil to read the second, 
then continue for each of the sentences. Ensure that pupils know the correct way 
to read each sentence.

activities.title: Comprehension questions— factual
activities.content:
Review the question word "Who"("hommbo")
• Read the question: 
• Say: Hommbo noddi ñawndoowo o nde Aadama nawni? jaabo: (Baaba Aadama noddi 
safroowo o nde Amada nawni)
• Ask pupils to answer the question. Give them feedback. 
• Ask pupils if they can tell you what the question word "hommbo" is asking about. 
Call on one or two pupils to respond. Let them know if they are correct, or incorrect 
and why. (Response: the question word  "hommbo"  asks us the name of a someone 
or something alive)
Teach pupils to use the question word ("hoto")
• Tell pupils that they will learn a new question word today, "hoto" Tell pupils that 
they will use it to answer the next question.                                                    
• Read the question: 
• Say: Siɗa nawni hoto yaata?
• Say: Helmere "hotto" haalanta en ko jaaboto  ɗeen koo fii dulaare maa ko woni. Simi 
nani "hotto" miɗo anndi jaabol ngol ko dulaa wonnta. 
• Read the question: 
• Say: Hoto Aadama wonno nde neene makko e baaba makko noddata mbo? Jaabawol: 
(Aadama na wonno ka suudu makko nde baaba makko e nene makko noddu noo 
mbo.)  
• Say: Fewtinen miijooji men ɗii e ko janngu ɗen koo. Taalol ngol wi'i: Mbo waalii  
haajooni
• Ask pupils to think about "hoto", or the place, that this happened.
• Call on pupils at random to respond.
• Read the question: Hoto baaba Aadama soodi sankee? 
 Jaabawol: ( ko ka marse  Babaa Aadama).

 Turn and Talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to talk about their answers 
to the question. Remind pupils that it is a "where" question.
 Call on a pupil to share their answer. Ask the rest of the class if they agree.

activities.title: Rapid review
activities.content:
Evaluate pupils use of the keyword "where" ("Hoto")
• Say: Lamndal adortee ngal: Ko helmere honnde heptinirten lamndi fii dula maa 
kowoni he taalol.
• Call on a pupil at random who raised their hand. Remind them that the word is 
"where" ( hoto).

sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Display mastery of key skills learned over the last four lessons: the parts of a book spaces between words and tracking a finger under print.

activities.title: Assessment
activities.content:
Special assessment - assess week 1 skills:
1.  Know what the "cover" and "back" of the book 
means.
2. Know that tracking a finger under  a word helps 
keep track of where you are reading.
1. Know what the "cover" and "back" of the book means.
• Hand out pupil books
• Tell pupils to hold up their books and point to the "front". Give feedback and explain. 
Give more examples if needed. If you see any pupil struggling, make sure to support 
them in this skill during the next lessons.
2. Understand that words in print are separated by spaces
• Ask pupils to turn to the first decodable story in their book. Show them the picture 
for the story, so they can find the story in the book. They will not be able to read this 
story yet, but that is alright. Do not ask them to read the story.
• Point to the "space" between the first two words in the story. Ask all pupils to put 
their finger on that space. Walk around and show them where to put their finger.
• Ask pupils to point to the next space in the story. Walk around to observe and give 
feedback.
• Ask pupils to raise their hand if they know what that space is for (why it's there). 
• Ask a volunteer to answer. Ask another pupil if the response is correct.
• Say: Jolɗe hankundere nde hollirat kelme ɗiɗe ɗe na serti. 
3. Know that tracking a finger under a word helps keep track of where you are 
reading

activities.title: Short and long vowel sound
activities.content:
Hear and see the short vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture on the page of the Pupil Book.
 Say: Hoɗum yiiɗon?

help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know.
 Say: Foɓɓen daaɗe ɗe he nde helmere (lama). Ko laabi jelu nanɗon hito/a/e helmere 
(lama)? Poɓɓen kadi. 
• Touch the letter in the Pupil Book. Say the sound. If pupils struggle to hear and say 
the sound, help them by saying another word with that sound in your language or 
another language they know.
• Say: Haalden helmere aroore nde-- (mama). On nani hito alkulal laaɓngal /a/ ka
• helmere (mama)? 
• Say: Jooni ko onon foti waɗde. Haale helmere nde. Fawe kolli mon ɗi ka alkulal "a"si 
ɗon waɗa hito /a/. 
Hear and see the long vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture in the next row on the Pupil Book page.
• Say: Mbo kala yo faw honndu mum e lees natal mbindaa ngal "kaba" ka lees.  
Say: Hoɗum yiiɗon? Ko "kaba"?
• Clap the syllables with the pupils.
 Say: Hito /a/ ngo no waawi fooɗeede . Siɗen haala hito ngo, en fooɗat hito ngo fii 
ngo juuta. On nani hito alkulal laaɓngal juutngal /aa/ e nder helmere nde "baaba"?
• Write the word on the chalk board. Point to the long vowel. Ask pupils to point to 
the same vowel in their book. Ask pupils how many of the letters of the day they see 
next to each other. Answer: two

long sound means that you stretch the sound longer when you say it.
• Demonstrate saying the short vowel sound and then the long vowel sound. Ask 
pupils to repeat. 
 Ensure that they can hear the difference between the short sound and the long 
(stretched) sound.

syllables and listen for the long vowel in the word.

activities.content:
Teach the letter

• Say: Ngal woni alkulal ngal hannde. Ngal waɗat hito /o/. kaalden ngal /o/
• Say: Ngal ko alkulal gootal ngal nii. Ngal waåat hito "O". Si ngal fuååima e helmere 
maa e innde, ko nii ngal wa'ata.
• Point to the capital letter "O" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Ngal ko alkulal gootal ngal nii.  Ngal waåata hito "O". Si ngal fuååima konngol 
maa e innde, ko nii ngal wa'ata.
• Point to the small letter "o" on the alphabet poster or on the board again.
• Say: "Most times, we will see it like this in words."
3. Short and long vowel sound  (15 mins)
Hear and see the short vowel within a word

• Point to the first picture on the page of the Pupil Book.
• Say: Ko hoåum yiiåon?
• Ask one pupil to name what is in the picture. Repeat the correct word. If needed, 
help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know.
• Say: Poêêen juuåe men fii fewnen daande nde /mo/to/. Laabi jelu nan åon /o/ e 
nder helmere nde "moto"? Foêêen juuåe men åe kadi.
• Touch the letter in the Pupil Book. Say the sound. If pupils struggle to hear and say 
the sound, help them by saying another word with that sound in your language or in 
another language they know.
• Say: Haalden  helmere aroyoonde nde: 'horde' On nani hito /o/  ka helmere 'horde'? 
Ko laabi jelu nanåoon ngo?"
Hear and see the long vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture in the next row on the Pupil Book page.
•  Say: O noon fof waɗee kolli mon ɗii ka lees natal sakkitingal ngal. Ko hoɗum yiiɗon? 
ɗum ko "boofo".
• Clap the syllables with the pupils.
• Say:/o/no waawi heɓde hito juut ngo. ɗum na firti si'en haali hito ngo en fooɗat ngo 
/oo/ fii ngo juuta. On nani hito /oo/ he helmere "boofo"
• Write the word on the chalk board. Point to the long vowel. Ask pupils to point to 
the same vowel in their book. Ask pupils how many of the letters of the day they see 
next to each other. Answer: two
• Tell pupils that when they see two "i" together, it makes a long sound/ii/. The long 
sound means that you stretch the sound longer when you say it.
• Demonstrate saying the short vowel sound and then the long vowel sound. Ask 
pupils to repeat. 
Ensure that they can hear the difference between the short sound and the long 
(stretched) sound.
• Continue in the same way using the next picture. Look at it, say the word, clap the 
syllables and listen for the long vowel in the word.

activities.content:

activities.title: At the beginning of this lesson, help pupils find the decodable story for this lesson. Instruct pupils who are not being assessed to read the story quietly. 2. Reason to Read
activities.content:

• Tell pupils that they will be reading a story with a partner while you work with 
individual pupil. 
• Say:  Ñannde wootere subaka, Aba na wonoo he dow saret mbabbi mbo yaha eɗen 
faala anndu hoto o yahatnoo.
• Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story in their Pupil 
Books.
• Tell pupils that they will see a few words in the story missing. With their partners, 
they should choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for 
the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to 
sit with you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).

• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more 
pupils sitting with the next pupil on the list.
• Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a 
general sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 
1-5 may indicate that the child is struggling. 
• Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A 
total of 40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider 
reinforcement activities for skill areas that are less than 40.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your coice on the skill(s) your pupils found 
challenging in the assessment, The skill reinforced by 
the activity is in the activity name: "Letter sound" or 
syllable blending"
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a 
pupil to say the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of 
a word that starts with the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share their words, then 
move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter 
sound that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table 
and quickly tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters 
that pupils have already learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that 
gets as many pupils to participate as possible, then gradually start saying letter 
sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards 
(try to use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a 
consonant and say its sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or 
have pupils say the sound). Ask pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the 
syllable made by the who flashcards. When they agree on the syllable, have them 
raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised their hands. Call on a 
pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of appreciation. 
Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the 
items aloud once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, 

slate, or other place. Call one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 
3 of the syllables they wrote down raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct 
items, they get a clap of appreciation from the class.

the picture on the page that matches that word. Ask all pupils to point to the next

the word for the class. Ask all pupils to point to the picture that matches the word.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to 
sit with you.

• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).

• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more 
pupils sitting with the next pupil on the list.
Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a 
general sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 
1-5 may indicate that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A 
total of 40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider 
reinforcement activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward

• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the 
beginning of the list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
1. Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skills(s) your pupils 
found challenging in the assessment. The skill 
reinforced by the activity is in te activity name: 
"letter sounds" or "syllable blending"
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a 
pupil to say the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of 
a word that starts with the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share their words, then 
move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter 
sound that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table 
and quickly tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that 
pupils have already learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets 
as many pupils to participate as possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds 
more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards 
(try to use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a 
consonant and say its sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or 
have pupils say the sound). Ask pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the 
syllable made by the who flashcards. When they agree on the syllable, have them 
raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised their hands. Call on a 
pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of appreciation. 
Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 

Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the 
items aloud once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, 
slate, or other place. Call one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 
3 of the syllables they wrote down raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct 
items, they get a clap of appreciation from the class.

2. Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)  (20 mins)
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to 
sit with you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).

• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more 
pupils starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).
Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a 
general sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 
1-5 may indicate that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
•  Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A 
total of 40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider 
reinforcement activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then sart over again from the 
beginning of the list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
1. Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your pupils 
found challenging in the assessment. The skill 
reinforced by the activity is in the activity name: 
"letter sounds" or "syllable blending".
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupil have learned but need to practice. Ask a pupil 
to say the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a 
word that starts with the sound. Call on 5-10 pupils to share their words, then move 
on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter 
sound that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table 
and quickly tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that 
pupils have already learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets 
as many pupils to participate as possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds 
more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards 
(try to use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a 
consonant and say its sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or 
have pupils say the sound). Ask pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the 
syllable made by the flashcards. When they agree on the syllable, have them raise 
their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised their hands. Call on a pair at 
random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of appreciation. Continue 
using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the 
items aloud once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, 
slate, or other place. Call one of the syllables at random. The first pupil hears all 

3 of the syllables they wrote down raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct 
items, they get a clap of appreciation from the class.

Blend letter sounds to read syllables and syllables to read words
Read syllables quickly and accurately

activities.title: Rapid letter review
activities.content:
Review small and capital letters
1. Point at random, quickly, to letters pupils have 
learned. Pupils say the sounds of the letters.  
aA, eE, iI, oO bB, kK, tT,

activities.title: Teach the sound
activities.content:
Tongue twister-say the sound
• Say the tongue twister. Pupils repeat.
• Cumooɓe cumi cete cabbi ceeɗu
• Ask pupils what sound they hear most.

Listening game - first sound 
• Say each word below. Pupils put a hand up if they hear the sound at the beginning 
of the word and on the desk if they do not.
Caabi taba cumi kaba cete baaba cabbi baa

activities.title: Letter and keyword
activities.content:
Teach the letter
• Point to the small letter "c" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Ko ngal woni alkulal men kesal hannde. Ngal alkulal wa åata hito /c/. kaalden 
ngal: /c/
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).

• Point to the capital letter "c" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: çum ko alkulal gortan ngal. Ngal wa åat hito/ c/. Si ngal woni he fuååorde 
konngol maa e innde, ko nii ngal wa'ata.
• Point to the small letter "c" on the alphabet poster or on the board again.
• Say: Ko heewi en yirat ngal nii he kelme
Keyword picture study
• Say: Ko hoåum njiiåon?
• Call on 1-2 pupils to name what they see in the picture.
• Say the keyword. Touch the letter of the day in the keyword in the pupil book. Say 
the sound. 
• Say: Haalden helmere: "caabi" . On nanii /c/ e nder helmere "caabi"?
• Ask pupils to touch the letter and say the word again. 
Keyword analysis (Pupil Book Box #1)
• Write the keyword from Box #1 on the board. 
• Point to the keyword.
• Say: Helmere ndee ko (caabi).
• Point to the syllable (under the keyword). Read it and show pupils how the syllable 
is part of the keyword.
• Point to the letter (under the syllable). Read it and show pupils how the letter is 
part of the syllable.

activities.title: Read syllables
activities.content:
Use the new letter sound to read syllables (Pupil Book Box #2)
• Write the Box #2 syllable column on the board. 
• Point to the first syllable. Cover the "aa" and show the "c".
• Say: Say: Ko woni ngoo hito? (pupils respond "c") 
• Cover the "c" and show the "aa".
• Say: Ko woni ngoo hito? (pupils respond "aa").
• Say: Oɗon mbaawi janngudu hitooji ɗi rentindiron ɗi, haalon daade. Jooni janngide
• hitooji ɗi kaaldon daade nde. /c/ /aa/, "caa" 

• Continue in this way for the other syllables/ Ask pupils to do the others. They will 
say each sound, and then the syllable. 
• After the pupils have read all the syllables together, give them 1 minute to try 
reading the syllables independently again from their books. 
Rapid syllable reading (Pupil Book Box #3)
• Write the first column of Box #3 on the board.
• Ask pupils, all together, to read down the column on the board. 
• Write each additional column, one at a time. Have pupils read the syllables in each 
column.
• Point to 5 syllables randomly. Ask the whole class to read each one quickly as you 
point to it. 

4. Read words  (10 mins)
Blending syllables to read words
• Write the first word on the chalkboard and help pupils find it in their books.
• Say: Hettoåe ndaaron. Mi janngat daaåe åe rentinonåe mbattonåe helmere.
• Model the blending process by reading each syllable, then blending the syllables 
together to read the word.
• Say: Ettoåen åum.
• Read the same syllables and the word, but this time with the pupils. Then ask the 
pupils to try the same word by themselves.
• Say: Jooni on ngnndii ko mbaɗaton. Jannge kelme ndeer defte mon kom no jannguduno 
ɗon ɗii: Ido ɗe jannge daaɗe ɗe. Ontuma kaalon helmere nde. Siɗon jannge pawon 
kolli monɗi e dow binndol he. (Monitor and help pupils.)
•  Call on 4 pupils at random to read one of the words using the blending process - 
reading the syllables, then the word. Provide help if needed.

sessions.title: Session B
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge of new and previously learned letters to read a short text independently
Make predictions using a picture
Write a new letter

activities.title: My language
activities.content:
Teach a rule of the language
1. Help pupils find my language picture box in the 
Pupil's Book.   
• Say: Siɗen haala maa eɗen hetto kelme e konngi he haala men, na waɗi sartaaji ɗi 
foɗɗen naftorde. çii sartaaji wallat yim êe faama kala ko haaletee. Janngen sarta 
kesal hannde.
• Say: Ko hoåum yiiåon ka natal?
• Say: Miåo ara haalde helmere maa mi janngakonngol. Hettoåe ko jagi. 
Mbabba
Mboobu
• Say: Ko hoåum faamåon he åee kelme? Ko hoåum åe firti?
• (Jaabawol: çee kelme åiåi fof na hollira huunde wootere. "Mbabba" ko innde kullal 
e ko mba woota.  
• Say: Ko helmere honnde holliri ko yiiåon ko ka natal?
• Call 1-2 learners to give similar examples of my language rules and explain what it 
means. Focus on my language examples on pupils' examples.

activities.title: Vocabulary – Before reading
activities.content:
Teach and discuss vocabulary.
• Write the vocabulary on the board (but not the definitions). Ask pupils what they 
know about each one.

• Discuss the word meaning, using gestures or illustrations to support understanding. 
If needed, help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they 
know. 
Haawnii
Mbeɗu alla

activities.title: Comprehension – Prediction
activities.content:
Prediction based on picture
• Help pupils find the decodable text of the day in their Pupil Books by holding up the 
page and saying the page number.
• Say: Ndaaree natal ngal! Ko njii ɗon? Ko cikkuɗon taalol ngol woni?
• Give pupils a moment to think, then invite them to share their predictions with a 
partner. Call on 2 pupils at random and ask for their predictions.

activities.title: Reason to read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Say: Jooni, on jannganat ko'e mon taalol he ndeer defte mon he. On mbaawi janngu 
kelme ngonɗe e taalol he sabu alkule ɗe en janngiinoɗe.
• Say: Ñalaande wootere Baaba mum Kummba yiɗno yaltude kono o yi'aani caabi 
beebee makko o. Eåen faala anndu hommbo okki mbo caabi åi. Janngen fii annden?
• Say: Liggore ko annduɗon he kuule alkule ɗee e daaɗe fii janngon  taalol ngol! 
Sappine kala helmere siɗon jannga taalol ngol.

activities.title: Decodable story reading – Independent
activities.content:
Pupils read aloud in the book independently.
• Ask pupils to read the decodable story independently. They should whisper read 
(read quietly), putting their finger under each word as they read it. If pupils finish 
reading early, they can read the story again with a partner.
• Walk around the classroom while pupils read. Help pupils use the skills they have 
learnt to read words. They should blend sounds to read syllables, and blend syllables 
to read words.

activities.title: Comprehension – Prediction check
activities.content:
Check prediction based on picture.

• Ask pupils to remember their predictions from before they read the story. Give them 
a moment to think. Ask them to raise their hands if their predictions were what 
happened in the story.
• Remind the class what the volunteer pupils predicted before they read the story. 
Ask the pupils if those predictions were what happened. 
6. Writing - Letters  (6 mins)
• Ask pupils to locate the letter "c" in a word in the decodable story. Call on 2 pupils 
at random to share the words they found.
• Write the letter " c" on the board (1/3 meter tall).
• Air write the letter (use a straight arm) and describe how to write the letter as you 
do it. Invite pupils to air write with you and say the sound. Watch them as they do 
it.
• Ask pupils to write the letter with a finger on their desks while saying the sound of 
the letter.
• Ask pupils to take out their exercise books and write the letter "c" 5 times.
• If some pupils finish early, tell them to draw a picture of something that begins with 
the sound / c/.

sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Separate syllables in spoken words
Use new words correctly in sentences
Make predictions using a title
Use verbal and nonverbal communication appropriately

activities.title: Clap the syllable
activities.content:
Tongue twister - blend syllables
1. Recite the tongue twister from yesterday.  
Cumooɓe cumi cete cabbi ceeɗu
Ask pupils what sound they hear most.
• Ask pupils what letter makes that sound.
• Clap the syllables of the tongue twister with pupils.
• Say: Jooni, mi haalat daaɗe dantang. Ndentindren kaalen helmere wootere immorde 
e fettol he.
• Say the syllables /cab/bi/ . Ask pupils to blend the syllables together to make a 
word from the tongue twister. (Answer: /caabi/
• Turn and talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them and say the word made by 
those syllables.
• Call on 1-2 pupils to say what word is made when they blend the syllables 
together.

activities.title: Vocabulary – before reading
activities.content:
Teach and discuss vocabulary
• Tell pupils each word. Have them repeat it. Talk to the pupils about the new words 
they will hear in the text. Ask pupils what they know about each one.
• Discuss with students the word meaning, using gestures or illustrations to support 
understanding.  
dammi
weltaare
ñiiwa

activities.title: Comprehension – Prediction
activities.content:
Prediction based on title
• Say: Miɗo ara janngu taalol. Mi haalanat on hoore taalol ngol. Mi yiɗat miijoɗon ko 
taalol ngol woni. Hoore taalol ngol woni. (Aba e Kummba).
• Turn and Talk: Ask pupils to turn a pupil next to them and make a guess (a prediction) 
about the story.
• Call on 2 pupils at random and ask them for their predictions.

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
Read the following story aloud (Use the pictures that goes with the story while 
reading)
• Ask pupils to do a thumbs up if they hear one of the new vocabulary words during 
the read aloud.
• Show the picture that goes with the story as you read aloud. While reading, pause 
to think aloud and talk to pupils about the story at key moments such as when you 
come to a vocabulary word the pupils just learned or when you hear a syllable the 
pupils just practiced.
Aba e Kummba
Ñannde wootere, Aba weetori. Baaba makko, Ablay wi'i, "Aba hannde hanaa a okkani 
ɓeyɗi ko ɗi ñaami?" Aba jaabi, "Mi taawi ɓe uddi damugal loobɓi ngu" Aba rewi he ndeer 
baali e beyåi ɗii o �ebti ton bofooje åe. Kummba ko miñirawo Aba. Kummba tawti Aba, 
fii wallugol mbo ñamin nde dammiåi. Kummba okki gertoåe åe kaaba. Aba okki beyåi e 
baali åi huåo. Dammiåi waåi dille weltaare. Kummba weltii, o wi'i "Dammi åi weltiima 
ko feewi!" Kummba lamndii Aba, "Si'en okkani dammiåi ñammri, hono åi waåata?" Aba 
wi'i, "çi mayat. Enen joggi ngurndam majji e toppitagol åi. Koåi dammi tann." Haajoni 
Aba wi'i, "Si ko kulle ladde ko wayno ñiiwa e njaba, åi topitono ko'e majji." "Kono enen 
topitoo dammi men ko wayno, beyi, baali e gertoo åe." Neene maêêe ari toon. O wi'i, 
"On topitiima dammiåi ko feewi. çi weltiima enen ne weltiåen."

activities.title: Comprehension – Prediction check
activities.content:
Check predictions based on title
• Remind the class what the volunteer pupil predicted before the read aloud. Ask the 
pupils if his prediction matched what was in the story.
• Ask the other pupils to think about what they predicted. Call on 2 pupils at random. 
Ask what they predicted, why, and if what they predicted is what happened in the 
story. 

5. Vocabulary - after reading  (5 mins)
Check for vocabulary understanding
• Ask pupils if they heard the new vocabulary words during the read aloud.
• Call on 3-4 pupils to say what vocabulary word they heard and to say the meaning 
in their own words.
• Say: Ƴepten kelme ɗe janngu ɗen ɗe mbaɗen kongi kesi.
• Give an example by using one of the words in a new sentence - a sentence that is 
not in the pupil book or read aloud.
• For each other vocabulary word introduced before reading, ask a pupil to use the 
word in a new sentence. Have pupils act out a word, if appropriate. Congratulate, 
help, or correct the pupils, depending on the responses.
• Remind pupils that they can use these words anytime throughout the day. Encourage 
pupils to share the words with their families at home.

activities.content:
Pupils read in pairs

activities.title: Comprehension – Factual questions
activities.content:
Ask factual questions
• Call on a pupil randomly to answer the following question:
• Lamndi: Ko hoɗum Bacci addi? Jabawol (Ko Caabi)
• After the response, congratulate, help, or correct the pupil's answer. If the pupil is 
partly correct or incorrect, tell them why. Help pupils find the sentence in the story 
that contains the answer. 
Ask inferential questions
• Ask each of the following questions. 
Question 1: : Ko hoko waɗi Bacci addi caabi o? Possible Answers: (O hoccu caabi o) 
• After each question, pupils talk in pairs about their answers. Call on a pupil randomly 
to share their answer to the question. Discuss their answers with the class. Help the 
pupils think about what is in the text or picture, as well as their own experiences, to 
reflect on what may have given them that idea.

activities.title: Writing – Story response
activities.content:
Pupils write or draw a response to the story
• Ask pupils to take out their exercise books.
• Ask pupils to write or draw their answer to the question "Ko hommbo jey jalo 
ngo?".

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)

• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more 
pupils starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).
Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a 
general sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 
1-5 may indicate that the child is struggling. 

Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A 
total of 40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider 
reinforcement activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the 
beginning of the list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
1. Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your pupils 
found challenging in the assessment. The skill 
reinforced by the activity is in the activity name: 
"letter sounds" or "syllable blending". 
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a 
pupil to say the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of 
a word that starts with the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share their words, then 
move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter 
sound that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table 
and quickly tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that 
pupils have already learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets 
as many pupils to participate as possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds 
more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards 
(try to use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a 
consonant and say its sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or 
have pupils say the sound). Ask pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the 
syllable made by the who flashcards. When they agree on the syllable, have them 
raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised their hands. Call on a 
pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of appreciation. 
Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 

Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the 
items aloud once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, 
slate, or other place. Call one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 
3 of the syllables they wrote down raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct 
items, they get a clap of appreciation from the class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to put their fingers under the first word in the word list for the activity 
in the pupil book. Read the first word.
• Say: Ko hoåum nde helmere firti?
• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point to 
the picture on the page that matches that word. Ask all pupils to point to the next 
word in the list and whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random to read 
the word for the class. Ask all pupils to point to the picture that matches the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.

activities.title: Word building
activities.content:

• Tell pupils they will write words using the syllables in the box.

• Ask pupils to point to the first syllable in the word on the Lesson 20 page in their 
Pupil Books. Then, write the syllable on the board.
• Continue asking pupils to point to the syllables in the word until the full word is 
written on the board.
• Say: Helmere nde ko "baaba" En mbindii helmere jooni. Janngiden nde.
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find 
the syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form 
the word in their copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next 
word. Continue with the rest of the words.
Words: baaba-/baa/ba/ booto-/boo/to/ kaba-/ beebee-/bee/bee/ cete-/ce/te/
Use syllables to build new words
• Say: Jooni, mi yid etoåon mbaååon kelme kese.
• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that 
they know and write it in their copy books.
• Turn and talk: When pupils are finished, ask them to turn to a pupil next to them to 
share the word they made.

activities.title: Letter and keyword
activities.content:
Teach the letter
• Point to the small letter "d" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Ko ngal woni alkulal men kesal ngal hannde. Ngal waɗat hito /d/. Haalden hito 
ngo /d/..
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).

• Point to the capital letter "D" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: çum ko alkulal gootal ngal. Ngal waɗat hito /d/. Si ngal woni fuɗɗorii konngol 
maa e innde, ko nii ngal wa'ata.  Point to the small letter "d" on the alphabet poster 
or on the board again.
• Say: Ko nii ngal woowi waa he kelme. 
Keyword picture study
• Say: Hoåum yii åon?
• Call on 1-2 pupils to name what they see in the picture.
• Say the keyword. Touch the letter of the day in the keyword in  the pupil book. 
Say the sound. 
• Say: Kaalden helmere: "diidi" . On nanii /d/ e ndeer helmere "diidi"?
• Ask pupils to touch the letter and say the word again. 
Keyword analysis (Pupil Book Box #1)
• Write the keyword from Box #1 on the board. 
• Point to the keyword.
• Say: Hoore helmere nde ko "diidi."
• Point to the syllable (under the keyword). Read it and show pupils how the syllable 
is part of the keyword.
• Point to the letter (under the syllable). Read it and show pupils  how the letter is 
part of the syllable.

activities.title: Read syllables
activities.content:
Use the new letter sound to read syllables (Pupil Book Box #2)
• Write the Box #2 syllable column on the board. 
• Point to the first syllable. Cover the "d" and show the "ii".
• Say: Hoko woni hito ngo (pupils respond "d") 
• Cover the "n" and show the "d".
• Say: Hoko woni hito ngo (pupils respond "d").
• Say: "Hiåon waawi janngide hitooji åii deen rentinonåi fii waåon daande. 
Janngiden hitooji åi jooni. /d/ /i/, "dii".  Continue in this way for the other 

syllables. Ask pupils to do the others. They will say each sound, and then the 
syllable. 
• After the pupils have read all the syllables together, give them 1 minute to try 
reading the syllables independently again from their books. 
Rapid syllable reading (Pupil Book Box #3)
• Write the first column of Box #3 on the board.
• Ask pupils, all together, to read down the column on the board. 
• Write each additional column, one at a time. Have pupils read the syllables in each 
column.
• Point to 5 syllables randomly. Ask the whole class to read each one quickly as you 
point to it.

activities.title: Read words
activities.content:
Blending syllables to read words
• Write the first word on the chalkboard and help pupils find it in their books.
• Say: Hettoåe nobete ndaaron. Mi janngat daaåe mi rentina åe fii mi waåa helmere.
• Model the blending process by reading each syllable, then blending the syllables 
together to read the word.
• Say: Ettoåen waåen åum.
• Read the same syllables and the word, but this time with the pupils. Then ask the 
pupils to try the same word by themselves.
• Say: Jooni on anndi ko waɗoton. Jannge kelme goɗɗe ɗe ka defte moon no wowirini. 
Fuɗɗore daaɗe ɗe ndeen janngon helmere nde. Memiree honndu mon ndu siɗon 
jannga. (Monitor and help pupils.)
• Call on 4 pupils at random to read one of the words using the blending process - 
reading the syllables, then the word. Provide help if needed.

Ask the pupils if those predictions were what happened.

the sound /d/.

activities.content:

activities.title: At the beginning of this lesson, help pupils find the decodable story for this lesson. Instruct pupils who are not being assessed to read the story quietly. 2. Reason to Read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story

individual pupils.
• Say: Ñalaande wootere Aba na jooɗinoo takka bitik defte mbo diida jooma bitik o, 
caggal ɗum jooma bitik o okki mbo kaba. Eɗen faala anndu ko kaba siifaa hoɗum 
okkki mbo. Janngen fii annden.
• Turn and talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story 
in their Pupil Books.
• Tell pupils that they will see a few words in the story missing. With their partners, 
they should choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for 
the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to 
sit with you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 

• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more 
pupils starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).
Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a 
general sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 
1-5 may indicate that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A 
total of 40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider 
reinforcement activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the 
beginning of the list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
1. Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your pupils 
found challenging in the assessment. The skill 
reinforced by the activity is in the activity name: 
"letter sounds" or "syllable blending".
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupil have learnt but need to practice. Ask a pupil 
to say the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a 
word that starts with the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share their words, then 
move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter 
sound that pupils have already learnt. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table 
and quickly tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that 
pupils have already learnt. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets 
as many pupils to participate as possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds 
more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards 
(try to use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a 
consonant and say its sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or 
have pupils say the sound). Ask pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the 
syllable made by the two flashcards. When they agree on the syllable, have them 
raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised their hands. Call on a 
pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of appreciation. 
Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo

• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learnt. Read the items 
aloud once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or 
other place. Call one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the 
syllables they wrote down raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they 
get a clap of appreciation from the class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to put their fingers under the first word in the word list for the activity 
in the pupil book. Read the first word.
• Say: Ko hoko ndee helmere firti?
• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point to 
the picture on the page that matches that word. Ask all pupils to point to the next 
word in the list and whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random to read 
the word for the class. Ask all pupils to point to the picture that matches the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.

activities.title: Word building
activities.content:
Use syllables to build given words
• Tell pupils they will write words using the syllables in the box. 
• Say: Miɗa miijoo helmere. Helmere ndee ko [diidi] poɓɓen nde [dii/di]
• Ask pupils to point to the first syllable in the word on the Lesson 20 page in their 
Pupil Book. Then, write the syllable on the board.
• Continue asking pupils to point to the syllables in the word until the full word is 
written on the board.
• Say: Helmere ndee ko "caabi" En keɓi helmere winndande. Janngiden helmere nde. 
(Pupils read the word)
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find 
the syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form 
the word in their copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next 
word. Continue with the rest of the words.
Words: cete-/ce/te/, kaba-/ka/ba/, diidi-/dii/di/ 
Use syllables to build new words
• Say: Jooni, miɗo yiɗi ettoɗon mbaɗon kelme!
• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that 
they know and write it in their copy books.
• Turn and talk: When pupils are finished, ask them to turn to a pupil next to them to 
share the word they made.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to 
sit with you.

• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).

• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more 
pupils starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).
Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a 
general sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 
1-5 may indicate that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A 
total of 40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider 
reinforcement activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the 
beginning of the list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
1. Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your pupils 
found challenging in the assessment. The skill 
reinforced by the activity is in the activity name: 
"letter sounds" or "syllable blending".
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
•  Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupil have learnt but need to practice. Ask a 
pupil to say the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of 
a word that starts with the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share their words, then 
move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter 
sound that pupils have already learnt. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table 
and quickly tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that 
pupils have already learnt. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets 
as many pupils to participate as possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds 
more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards 
(try to use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a 
consonant and say its sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or 
have pupils say the sound). Ask pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the 
syllable made by the who flashcards. When they agree on the syllable, have them 
raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised their hands. Call on a 
pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of appreciation. 
Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 

Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learnt. Read the items 
aloud once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or 
other place. Call one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the 
syllables they wrote down raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they 
get a clap of appreciation from the class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:

in the pupil book. Read the first word.
• Say: Ko hoåum nde helmere firti?
• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point to 
the picture on the page that matches that word. Ask all pupils to point to the next 
word in the list and whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random to read 
the word for the class. Ask all pupils to point to the picture that matches the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.

activities.title: Word building
activities.content:

• Ask pupils to point to the first syllable in the word on the Lesson 20 page in their 
Pupil Books. Then, write the syllable on the board.
• Continue asking pupils to point to the syllables in the word until the full word is 
written on the board.
• Say: Helmere nde ko "mbabba" En mbindii helmere nde jooni. Janngiden nde. (Pupils 
read the word)
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find 
the syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form 
the word in their copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next 
word. Continue with the rest of the words.
Words: moto-/mo/to/, baaba-/baa/ba/, diidii-/dii/di/, bitik-/bi/tik/ 
Use syllables to build new words
• Say: Jooni, mi yid etoåon mbaååon kelme kese.

• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that 
they know and write it in their copy books.
• Turn and talk: When pupils are finished, ask them to turn to a pupil next to them to 
share the word they made.

activities.title: Read syllables
activities.content:

• Say: Hoko woni hito ngo?   (pupils respond "f")

hitooji åi jooni. /j/ /a/, "ja".  
• Continue in this way for the other syllables. Ask pupils to do the others. They will 
say each sound, and then the syllable. 
• After the pupils have read all the syllables together, give them 1 minute to try 

reading the syllables independently again from their books. 
Rapid syllable reading (Pupil Book Box #3)
• Write the first column of Box #3 on the board.

• Write each additional column, one at a time. Have pupils read the syllables in each

• Point to 5 syllables randomly. Ask the whole class to read each one quickly as you 
point to it. 
4. Read words  (10 mins)

• Say: Hettoɗe nobete ndaaron. Mi janngat daaɗe mi rentina ɗe fii mi waɗa helmere.

together to read the word.
• Say: Ettoåen waåen åum

pupils to try the same word by themselves.
• Say: Jooni on anndi ko waɗoton. Jannge kelme goɗɗe ɗe ka defte mon no wowirini.
• Fuɗɗore daaɗe ɗe ndeen janngong helmere nde. Memiree kollli mon ɗi siɗon jannga.
• (Monitor and help pupils.)
• Call on 4 pupils at random to read one of the words using the blending process - 
reading the syllables, then the word. Provide help if needed.

reading the syllables independently again from their books.

point to it.

activities.content:
Prepare for the assessment
1. Prepare an assessment page in a notebook. List

"syllables" and "individual score".

activities.title: At the beginning of this lesson, help pupils find the decodable story for this lesson. Instruct pupils who are not being assessed to read the story quietly. 2. Reason to Read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Tell pupils that they will be reading a story with a partner while you work with 
individual pupils.
• Say: Aba ko heede jakka o ho åi, ko baaba makko jogii caabi jakka o. kono Ñalaade 
wotere Baaba makko waawaano yaade ka jakka. Eden faala anndu de ko hommbo 
addino mbo caabi jakka o ndeen ñalaande. Janngen fii annden. Say: Janngenfii 
annden hoêe woni sukaaêe makko êe.
• Turn and talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story 
in their Pupil Books.
• Tell pupils that they will see a few words in the story missing. With their partners, 
they should choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for 
the story.
2. Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads 
in pairs)  (2 mins)
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to 
sit with you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 

• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more 
pupils starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).
Score the assessment - for each pupil
•  Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives 
a general sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 
1-5 may indicate that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A 
total of 40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider 
reinforcement activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the 
beginning of the list. 
2. Comprehension - Comprehension questions  (6 mins)
Ask comprehension questions
• Thank pupils for staying on task and working well with their partners.
• Call on a pupil randomly to answer each of the following questions:
Question 1: Ko hommbo woni remoowo? Jaabawol: Daado
Question 2: Ko hoko waåi êe rema ka faro?
• After each response, congratulate, help, or correct the pupil's answer. If the pupil 
is partly correct or incorrect, tell them why. Help pupils find the sentence in the 
story that contains the answer.

activities.title: Reinforcement activitiesn
activities.content:
NOTE
1. Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your pupils 
found challenging in the assessment. The skill 
reinforced by the activity is in the activity name: 
"letter sounds" or "syllable blending"..

Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learnt but need to practice. Ask a pupil 
to say the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a 
word that starts with the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share their words, then 
move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter 
sound that pupils have already learnt. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table 
and quickly tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that 
pupils have already learnt. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets 
as many pupils to participate as possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds 
more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards 
(try to use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a 
consonant and say its sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or 
have pupils say the sound). Ask pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the 
syllable made by the two flashcards. When they agree on the syllable, have them 
raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised their hands. Call on a 
pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of appreciation. 
Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 

Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learnt. Read the items 
aloud once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or 
other place. Call one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the 
syllables they wrote down raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they 
get a clap of appreciation from the class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to put their fingers under the first word in the word list for the activity 
in the pupil book. Read the first word.
• Say: Ko hoåum nde helmere firti?
• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point to 
the picture on the page that matches that word. Ask all pupils to point to the next 
word in the list and whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random to read 
the word for the class. Ask all pupils to point to the picture that matches the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck. 
2. Word building  (10 mins)
Use syllables to build given words
• Tell pupils they will write words using the syllables in the box. 
• Say: Miɗo mijoo helmere. Helmere nde ko "jakka". Foɓɓiden daaɗe ɗe /jak/ ka/.
• Ask pupils to point to the first syllable in the word on the Lesson 20 page in their 
Pupil Books. Then, write the syllable on the board.
• Continue asking pupils to point to the syllables in the word until the full word is 
written on the board.
• Say: Helmere nde ko "mbabba" En mbindii helmere nde   jooni. Janngiden nde.
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find 
the syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form 
the word in their copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next 
word. Continue with the rest of the words.
Words: beebee /bee/bee/, kaba /ka/ba/,  moto /mo/to/, cete /ce/te/  
Use syllables to build new words
• Say: Jooni, mi yid etoåon mbaååon kelme kese.
• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that 
they know and write it in their copy books.
• Turn and talk: When pupils are finished, ask them to turn to a pupil next to them to 
share the word they made.
